This article analyzes the distribution of surgical interventions performed on patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), categorized under indicator 6 in the Danish IBD registry [^src1]. The data provides a comprehensive breakdown of specific procedure codes, their absolute counts, and their respective percentages of the total surgical volume [^src1]. 

Because the dataset represents a single cross-sectional snapshot from the 2025 report, no longitudinal trends regarding the shifting popularity or phasing out of specific surgical techniques can be established [^src1]. Furthermore, the table does not define specific clinical targets, thresholds, or performance standards, meaning the data cannot be evaluated against a met or missed benchmark [^src1].

The most frequently performed specific procedure is [[kjfh11-laparoskopisk-kolektomi-og-ileostomi|KJFH11]] (laparoscopic colectomy and ileostomy), accounting for 135 operations or 9.1% of the total [^src1]. It is closely followed by [[kjfb21-laparoskopisk-ileocokal-resektion|KJFB21]] (132 cases, 8.9%) and [[kjah01-laparoskopi|KJAH01]] (130 cases, 8.7%) [^src1]. The fourth and fifth most common interventions are [[kjah00-eksplorativ-laparotomi|KJAH00]] (120 cases, 8.1%) and [[kjfg40-revision-af-enterostomi-el-kolostomi-u-laparotomi|KJFG40]] (88 cases, 5.9%) [^src1]. Together, these top five specific procedures represent a substantial portion of the surgical workload. Other notable procedures include [[kjfb00-tyndtarmsresektion|KJFB00]] (small bowel resection), which was performed 86 times (5.8%) [^src1].

At the lower end of the spectrum, several specialized or less frequent procedures trail the list with only 5 recorded cases each (0.3%), including laparostomy (KJAH30), other laparoscopic colon resections (KJFB51), sigmoid resections with colostomy (KJFB60), proctocolectomy and ileostomy (KJFH20), and reoperations for superficial infections (KJWB00) [^src1]. 

A significant outlier in the dataset is the "Øvrige" (Other) category, which aggregates 152 procedures, making it the single largest grouping at 10.2% of all interventions [^src1]. This indicates that while the registry tracks dozens of specific surgical codes in detail, a notable fraction of IBD-related surgeries fall into miscellaneous or less standardized classifications.
